title: How to Sort and Filter Data in Excel
dek: To sort in Excel, select your table and use Data > Sort; to filter, use Data > Filter and pick which rows to show. Sorting reorders your data, filtering hides rows without deleting them. Here is how to do both, step by step.

richText: Sorting and filtering are the two fastest ways to make sense of a long list in Excel. Sorting reorders the rows — alphabetically, or from highest to lowest. Filtering hides the rows you do not want to see right now, without deleting anything. Learn both and even a huge sheet becomes easy to read.

In the Sort dialog, keep "My data has headers" ticked, choose the column, and set the order. Click "Add Level" for a second column (for example, sort by Region, then by Sales).

body.richText: Do not select a single column before sorting. If you highlight only one column and sort it, Excel may move just those values while the other columns stay put — scrambling your rows. Click one cell and let Excel take the whole table, or select the full range including headers.

items.question: What is the difference between sorting and filtering in Excel?
items.answerRichText: Sorting reorders every row — for example, alphabetically or highest to lowest. Filtering hides the rows you do not want to see, without changing or deleting anything. Use sorting to rank data and filtering to focus on part of it.

items.question: How do I sort by more than one column in Excel?
items.answerRichText: On the Data tab, click Sort to open the Sort dialog, then use "Add Level" to stack columns. Excel sorts by the first level, then breaks ties with the next — for example, sort by Region, then by Sales within each region.

items.question: Why did sorting mix up my rows?
items.answerRichText: You probably selected a single column instead of the whole table. Sorting one column moves only its values while the rest stay put. Click one cell and let Excel take the full table, or select the entire range with headers so whole rows move together.

items.question: What is the keyboard shortcut for filter in Excel?
items.answerRichText: Press Ctrl+Shift+L to turn AutoFilter on or off. It adds or removes the drop-down arrows on your headers instantly, without going to the Data tab.
